The double-debit is real in code: cancel() computes sharesToRemove = D - V*D/T without subtracting schedule.released, so a soft schedule that released then cancels debits those shares twice from _totalTokenShares. It requires the attacker to be the creator of the soft schedule and to own a receiver schedule in the same pool.

Pass2's 1:1 observation is confirmed for VEK (250M/250M), AXGT (125.7M/125.7M), old-AXGT (95M/95M) and OXN (807.5M/807.5M) at block 26,229,646. A 1:1 pool is healthy: release pays exactly relShares*balance/totalShares, no premium (fork test F).

Only 6 of 76 ETH pools are not 1:1: EDGEN, ZC, pepecoin, LO0P (the Oct-14-attacked pools) and two small pools. EDGEN has totalShares=17,572,899 vs balance=32,941,964,644 wei, so the 0xcc5d4c9d schedules' nominal claims (up to 2.56e26 wei) exceed the pool and release reverts.
The only live soft+topable ETH schedule (5063) is the Oct-14 attacker's, fully released (released == T == 127,340.97e18), claim 0, token pepecoin, pool 288.9 PEPE.

34 ETH schedules are NFTized and 10 are transferable. Fork test E transfers soft NFT 4972 to a fresh attacker: beneficiary becomes the attacker, creator stays 0x1137da98..., release pays the exact pro-rata claim, cancel/topUp revert NotAuthorized.
BSC: 66 live soft+topable schedules, all creator/beneficiary 0x8174eee3af07c9a695ca363a38dc3190f6dd0dec (the Oct-14 helper), all claim 0; the BTCLE pool is dust. They are a re-arm monitor only.

Nominal $4.18M ETH: VEK $2.50M (no DEX pair), AXGT $0.94M ($154k pool), old-AXGT $0.23M (no pair), OXN $0.34M (no pair), TCT $0.076M ($32k pool). Hard realizable if the bug were reachable: approx $46.6k-$93.2k ETH; BSC approx $18.9k-$37.8k; combined approx $65.5k-$131.0k.

Conditional re-arm: one owner tx setFlatFee(<payable>) or setCreatorFeeExempt/setTokenFeeExempt. Fork test H proves create/release/cancel work with flatFee=0 and feePercentage=0 on a mock token; the immutable bug is intact.

cancel() on a fully vested fee-paying schedule reverts with arithmetic underflow (T is net of the token fee, getVestedAmount is gross). This is an additional blocker for the residual attacker schedules: they need a top-up to a future tranche before cancel, and the pools are dust.
caveats: Point-in-time reads at ETH block 26,229,646 and BSC block 128,639,266 (2026-10-20); re-verify before acting.
The 25%-50%-of-DEX-depth realizable bound is an estimate; the true impact of selling 125.7M AXGT into a $154k pool is likely at the low end.
Blockscout marks for VEK/old-AXGT/OXN are not backed by any DEX pair; they are reported only to reconcile pass2's nominal $4.18M and are marked $0 hard.
BSC nominal $1.48M is pass2/prior GoldRush marks; only DROPS and LOOPRA have observable pairs today. BscScan's own net-worth figure was ~$45.7k at the ZH3 read.
The owner Safe can re-arm the immutable bug with one parameter transaction; that is P-class and monitored, not E-U.
No mainnet transaction was signed or sent; all PoC work is a read-only Foundry fork.
one_liner: External unprivileged attacker can extract $0 live: release() is beneficiary-gated and cancel()/topUp() are creator-gated, so a fresh attacker cannot obtain the roles needed for the shared-pool double-debit; creation is blocked by flatFee=uint256.max on ETH and 35,000 BNB on BSC with zero exemptions, and no live soft+topable schedule has a positive claim in a funded pool — the pass2 'permissionless release' correction is rejected, and its $5.7M is nominal (hard realizable only ~$65k-$131k if the bug were re-armed).
